paper.title: Absolute continuity of invariant measures for random diffeomorphisms
paper.abstract: We develop criteria showing that invariant measures for random walks generated by diffeomorphisms of manifolds are in the Lebesgue class. Our assumptions are first, that there is a uniform expansion gap in the Lyapunov spectrum of the random walk, and second, that the conditionals of the invariant measure along the appropriate (partial) stable manifolds are in the Lebesgue class.

analysis.relevance_note: Absolute continuity of invariant measures and partial stable-manifold conditionals provide a substantial connection to ergodic and smooth dynamics.
analysis.tldr: The authors give criteria ensuring that invariant measures for random walks generated by manifold diffeomorphisms belong to the Lebesgue class.
analysis.problem: Determine when an invariant measure for a random walk generated by diffeomorphisms is in the Lebesgue class.
analysis.main_result: The criteria assume a uniform expansion gap in the random walk’s Lyapunov spectrum and that the invariant measure’s conditionals along the appropriate partial stable manifolds are in the Lebesgue class. Under these assumptions the invariant measure itself is in the Lebesgue class. The precise formulation of the expansion gap and choice of partial stable manifolds: Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: Random diffeomorphisms, invariant measures, Lyapunov spectra and stable manifolds.

paper.title: On exponential stability of generalized linear functional differential equations
paper.abstract: We develop a general approach to uniform exponential stability for a broad class of linear functional differential equations with Volterra operators. The considered class includes delay differential equations, integro-differential equations, equations with distributed delays, vector equations, and systems of scalar functional differential equations. Standard assumptions on the equation are relaxed to include measurable parameters. Some results remain valid for equations with unbounded delays and oscillatory coefficients and kernels. For all the above mentioned classes of equations, explicit uniform exponential stability tests are obtained.

analysis.relevance_note: The focus is exponential stability tests for functional differential equations, without a central entropy, dimension, symbolic or group-action component.

paper.title: Marchal-type lemmas for the restricted $(N+1)$-body problem with their applications
paper.abstract: The direct methods of calculus of variations have had a great success in the classical Newtonian $N$-body problem in this century. First in finding periodic solutions and more recently in the existence of parabolic, hyperbolic and hyperbolic-parabolic solutions. The foundation of many of these results is Marchal's lemma, which guarantee's fixed-end local minimizers are collision-free and hence classical solutions of the $N$-body problem. Meanwhile almost no result is available in the restricted problem through the direct methods of calculus of variations, mainly due to the lack of a Marchal-type lemma. In this paper such a lemma and its variation will be obtained for the restricted problem. We then apply them to the restricted problem to study unbounded (hyperbolic, parabolic, bi-hyperbolic and bi-parabolic) solutions, and bounded (periodic and quasi-periodic) solutions. We emphasize that the extension to the restricted case does not follow from the standard arguement for the unrestricted case.

analysis.relevance_note: Periodic, quasiperiodic and unbounded celestial trajectories give a possible connection to geometric dynamics, although the abstract does not state an entropy, dimension or symbolic result.
analysis.tldr: The authors obtain a Marchal-type lemma and a variation for the restricted body problem, then apply them to bounded and unbounded solutions.
analysis.problem: Develop a Marchal-type foundation for applying direct variational methods to the restricted body problem.
analysis.main_result: The authors establish a restricted-problem version of Marchal’s lemma and a variation, and apply them to hyperbolic, parabolic, bi-hyperbolic and bi-parabolic unbounded solutions, as well as periodic and quasiperiodic bounded solutions. They emphasize that the extension does not follow from the usual unrestricted argument. Exact hypotheses of the new lemmas and detailed existence statements: Not specified in the abstract.
methods: Direct methods of calculus of variations
analysis.context: Celestial mechanics, variational methods and bounded or unbounded trajectories.

paper.title: Continuity of biaccessibility dimension for polynomials
paper.abstract: For a polynomial $f$ of degree $d\geq 2$, its biaccessible set $B(f)$ consists of angles whose external rays are smooth and land at a point receiving at least two smooth external rays. We prove that the function $f\mapsto {\rm dim}_H(B(f))$ is continuous on the entire space of degree-$d$ polynomials. Therefore $(\log d){\rm dim}_H (B(f))$ gives a continuous extension of classical core entropy from the postcritically finite case to all polynomials of degree $d$.

analysis.relevance_note: Hausdorff dimension and core entropy are central, directly matching the strongest dimensional and entropy interests.
analysis.tldr: For polynomials of any fixed degree at least two, the Hausdorff dimension of the biaccessible angle set varies continuously across the entire parameter space. Multiplication by the logarithm of the degree therefore extends classical core entropy continuously beyond postcritically finite polynomials.
analysis.problem: For a degree-\(d\) polynomial \(f\), study the parameter dependence of the Hausdorff dimension of \(B(f)\), the angles whose external rays are smooth and land at a point receiving at least two smooth external rays.
analysis.main_result: For every fixed \(d\geq2\), the map \(f\mapsto\dim_H B(f)\) is continuous on the entire space of degree-\(d\) polynomials. Consequently, \((\log d)\dim_H B(f)\) is a continuous extension of classical core entropy from the postcritically finite case to all degree-\(d\) polynomials.
analysis.context: Polynomial dynamics, external rays, Hausdorff dimension and core entropy.

paper.title: Rigorous verification of period-doubling bifurcations in maps
paper.abstract: We present a computer-assisted approach for proving period-doubling bifurcations in one-parameter families of maps $x \mapsto f(x,\lambda)$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$. We solve a square augmented system, called the period-doubling map, whose unknowns are the fixed point, the parameter, the right eigenvector attached to the eigenvalue $-1$, the left eigenvector with its eigenvalue, and the vector which describes the center manifold to second order. A contraction argument gives a solution close to a numerical approximation, at which the Jacobian is invertible. The determinant of this Jacobian factors into a simple expression, so that it is nonzero exactly when $1$ is not an eigenvalue and $-1$ is a simple eigenvalue crossing the unit circle transversally. Apart from the sign of the cubic normal-form coefficient, computed afterwards, it remains to check with Gershgorin disks that no other eigenvalue lies on the unit circle. The method is applied to a $10$-mode Galerkin projection of the Kot--Schaffer growth-dispersal model, for which we prove a supercritical period-doubling bifurcation.

analysis.relevance_note: The focus is computer-assisted verification of period-doubling bifurcations and a numerical model application, without a central connection to the strongest interests.

paper.title: A note on the non-wandering dynamics in the $n$-fold symmetric products
paper.abstract: We construct a homeomorphism on a compact metric space whose non-wandering set consists of a single fixed point, while the induced map $F_n(f)$ possesses infinitely many (non-fixed) non-wandering points.

analysis.relevance_note: Non-wandering sets of induced maps on symmetric products are central questions in topological dynamics.
analysis.tldr: The authors construct a compact-metric-space homeomorphism with a single fixed non-wandering point whose induced symmetric-product map has infinitely many non-fixed non-wandering points.
analysis.problem: Compare the non-wandering dynamics of a homeomorphism with those of its induced map on an n-fold symmetric product.
analysis.main_result: There exists a homeomorphism on a compact metric space whose non-wandering set is a single fixed point, while the induced map \(F_n(f)\) has infinitely many non-fixed non-wandering points. The admissible values of \(n\) and details of the construction: Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: Topological dynamics, induced maps and non-wandering sets.

paper.title: Generalization of Navascu\'es' $\alpha$-fractal operator on lifted Sierpi\'nski gasket
paper.abstract: The primary objective of the present article is to extend Navascu\'es' class of $\alpha$-fractal interpolation functions ($\alpha$-FIFs) from a Euclidean domain to a non-Euclidean domain. Precisely, we consider the lifted Sierpi\'nski gasket $\big(\widetilde{SG}\big)$, which is a subset of the first Heisenberg group equipped with a \textit{non-Euclidean metric} (popularly known as the Heisenberg metric), and demonstrate the existence of the class of $\alpha$-FIFs in the continuous space on $\widetilde{SG}$. Subsequently, we derive certain conditions on the parameters so that the same class lies in the H\"{o}lder space on $\widetilde{SG}$. Next, we extend the theory of Navascu\'es' $\alpha$-fractal operator from the Euclidean space to the Heisenberg space, and we also report several properties of the same operator. Additionally, we discuss certain dimensional results of the graphs of the functions with respect to the Heisenberg metric besides the Euclidean metric. We also cover some of the dimensional preserving and the set-valued results corresponding to the dimension of the graphs of the functions.

analysis.relevance_note: Fractal interpolation and graph dimensions in Euclidean and Heisenberg metrics are central dimensional and fractal-geometric topics.
analysis.tldr: The authors extend the stated class of fractal interpolation functions and its operator to the lifted Sierpiński gasket in the first Heisenberg group. They also obtain Hölder-space conditions and graph-dimension results in two metrics.
analysis.problem: Extend Navascués’ fractal interpolation theory from Euclidean domains to the lifted Sierpiński gasket with the Heisenberg metric, and study regularity and graph dimensions.
analysis.main_result: The authors establish existence of the class of \(\alpha\)-fractal interpolation functions in the continuous-function space on the lifted gasket and give parameter conditions ensuring Hölder regularity. They extend the \(\alpha\)-fractal operator to Heisenberg space and discuss operator properties, graph dimensions in the Heisenberg and Euclidean metrics, dimension-preserving results and set-valued results. The exact parameter conditions and dimensional formulas: Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: Fractal interpolation on a lifted Sierpiński gasket and metric-dependent graph dimensions.

paper.title: Critical cusp cancellation and analytic response for a Bernoulli random interval map
paper.abstract: We show that the critical cusp exponent $\beta=-1/2$ admits $W^{2,1}$ invariant densities in an explicit family of expanding full-branch interval maps. The usual estimates exclude this exponent because two zero-order coefficients in the second derivative of the transfer operator are individually non-integrable. Their signed combination, however, contains the factor $\beta(2\beta+1)$ for a pure power cusp. We exploit its cancellation at $\beta=-1/2$ to prove a $W^{2,1}$ Lasota--Yorke inequality and a spectral gap for the explicit family. We also identify a separate obstruction caused by an interior cusp value. As an application, a small Bernoulli probability perturbation between two fixed maps has a stationary density that depends real-analytically on the perturbation parameter in $W^{2,1}$, with explicit formulas for all response derivatives.

analysis.relevance_note: Transfer-operator spectral gaps, invariant densities and analytic response provide a substantial connection to ergodic dynamics.
analysis.tldr: For an explicit family of expanding full-branch interval maps, cancellation at the cusp exponent \(\beta=-1/2\) permits \(W^{2,1}\) invariant densities and a spectral gap. Small Bernoulli probability perturbations between two fixed maps have a real-analytic stationary-density response in that space.
analysis.problem: Establish transfer-operator estimates at the critical cusp exponent \(\beta=-1/2\), where the usual separate estimates of two zero-order coefficients in the second derivative are non-integrable.
analysis.main_result: For a pure power cusp, the signed combination of those coefficients contains \(\beta(2\beta+1)\), which vanishes at \(\beta=-1/2\). The authors exploit this to prove a \(W^{2,1}\) Lasota-Yorke inequality and spectral gap for the explicit family, while identifying a separate obstruction from an interior cusp value. They obtain real-analytic dependence of the stationary density on a small Bernoulli probability perturbation in \(W^{2,1}\), with formulas for all response derivatives. The explicit family and response formulas: Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: Expanding interval maps, stationary densities and analytic response.

paper.title: Orthogonal Projections and Assouad Dimension: Resolving Fraser's Questions
paper.abstract: We examine two questions on exceptional orthogonal projections for Assouad dimension. Let $1\le k<d$ and $1\le q<d$. For a set $F$ contained in a $q$-dimensional subspace $W\subset\R^d$ and containing a nonempty relatively open subset of $W$, we compute both the Hausdorff and packing dimensions of the exceptional $k$-planes as $k(d-k)-|q-k|-1$. In particular, a square in $\R^3$ has a one-dimensional set of exceptional plane projections. This disproves the bound $k(d-1-k)$ in Question 17.8.1 of Fraser's book as stated, for every $2\le k<d$. The planar packing question, Question 17.8.2, is already answered affirmatively by Wu's countability theorem. Using that theorem, we also describe the distinction between planar sets of Assouad dimension at most $1$ and those of dimension greater than $1$ when they are embedded in higher-dimensional spaces. The computations use elementary Grassmannian geometry; we make no claim of a new planar projection theorem or of an optimal bound for arbitrary higher-dimensional sets.

analysis.relevance_note: Exceptional projections and Hausdorff, packing and Assouad dimensions directly match the strongest fractal-dimension interests.
analysis.tldr: The authors compute Hausdorff and packing dimensions of exceptional projection planes for sets containing relative interior in a linear subspace, disproving a stated higher-dimensional bound. They distinguish this calculation from the already settled planar question and make no general optimality claim.
analysis.problem: Examine two questions about exceptional orthogonal projections for Assouad dimension, including a proposed higher-dimensional bound and a planar packing question.
analysis.main_result: Let \(1\leq k<d\), \(1\leq q<d\), and let \(F\) lie in a \(q\)-dimensional subspace \(W\subset\mathbb R^d\) and contain a nonempty relatively open subset of \(W\). Both the Hausdorff and packing dimensions of the exceptional \(k\)-planes equal \(k(d-k)-|q-k|-1\). A square in \(\mathbb R^3\) has a one-dimensional exceptional set of plane projections; the authors disprove the bound \(k(d-1-k)\) in Question 17.8.1 as stated for every \(2\leq k<d\). Wu’s countability theorem already answers the planar packing question affirmatively and is used to distinguish embeddings of planar sets with Assouad dimension at most one from those of larger dimension. The authors claim neither a new planar projection theorem nor an optimal bound for arbitrary higher-dimensional sets.
analysis.context: Fractal dimensions, exceptional projections and Grassmannian geometry.

paper.title: Finiteness of planar central configurations of six bodies for all positive masses: Part I, exceptional-mass first limits
paper.abstract: We separate the generic positive-mass finiteness problem for planar six-body central configurations from finiteness on exceptional mass loci. The Chang--Chen diagram enumeration has 117 graphs. The arguments below confine 40 first-limit diagram obligations to proper necessary mass loci. In particular, a direct function-field argument establishes the No.~66 mass condition for both zero and nonzero drift. We establish the algebraic reduction from an infinite positive family to a germ with an unbounded seven-product, and use the stated diagram rules and computational certificates to confine its mass vector to the union of these loci. Finiteness on the exceptional positive mass loci, the proposed subject of Part II, will be discussed in another paper.

analysis.relevance_note: The focus is algebraic finiteness reductions for six-body central configurations and exceptional mass loci, without a central connection to the strongest interests.

paper.title: A holomorphic motion with non-subharmonic Hausdorff dimension
paper.abstract: We present an example of a holomorphic motion of a Cantor set $\lambda \mapsto A_\lambda$ for which neither the Hausdorff dimension $\dimH(A_\lambda)$ nor the lower Minkowski dimension $\dimMl(A_\lambda)$ is a subharmonic function of~$\lambda$. This answers negatively a question of Fuhrer--Ransford--Younsi, and distinguishes these dimensions from packing and upper Minkowski dimensions, for which subharmonicity holds. All four dimensions are computed explicitly.

analysis.relevance_note: Variation of Hausdorff and Minkowski dimensions of Cantor sets is central to the fractal-dimension profile.
analysis.tldr: The authors construct a holomorphic motion of a Cantor set for which neither Hausdorff dimension nor lower Minkowski dimension is subharmonic in the motion parameter.
analysis.problem: Determine whether Hausdorff dimension and lower Minkowski dimension must vary subharmonically under a holomorphic motion of a Cantor set.
analysis.main_result: The example \(\lambda\mapsto A_\lambda\) answers the Fuhrer-Ransford-Younsi question negatively: neither \(\dim_H A_\lambda\) nor the lower Minkowski dimension is subharmonic in \(\lambda\). This contrasts with packing and upper Minkowski dimensions, for which the abstract states subharmonicity holds. All four dimensions are computed explicitly; their formulas and the construction details: Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: Holomorphic motions, Cantor sets and parameter dependence of fractal dimensions.

paper.title: Bounded Leaf Volumes and Analytic Quotients of Singular Holomorphic Foliations
paper.abstract: Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a singular holomorphic foliation of dimension $k$ on a compact K\"ahler manifold $M$ of dimension $n$. Suppose that the volumes of its regular leaves are uniformly bounded, $\dim(Sing\mathcal{F})<k$, and the union of the leaf closures meeting $Sing\mathcal{F}$ has finite $2k$-dimensional Hausdorff measure. We prove that the quotient by chains of intersecting leaf closures is a normal compact complex analytic space of dimension $n-k$. The quotient map is proper and holomorphic, with connected fibers. The proof uses Bishop's theorems, Remmert and Stein extension, Barlet's cycle space, and Stein factorization. Away from the images of separatrices, the quotient has local charts given by finite holonomy groups. Examples show that these images need not coincide with the singular set of the quotient, and that bounded leaf volumes alone do not imply Hausdorffness. In codimension one, Malgrange's theorem makes the separatrix measure assumption automatic when $codim(Sing\mathcal{F})\geq 3$.

analysis.relevance_note: Leaf-closure quotients, holonomy and Hausdorffness provide a substantial topological connection within holomorphic foliation theory.
analysis.tldr: Under bounded-volume, singular-set and separatrix-measure assumptions, the quotient by chains of intersecting leaf closures is a normal compact complex analytic space with a proper holomorphic quotient map and connected fibers.
analysis.problem: Determine when the leaf-closure quotient of a singular holomorphic foliation on a compact Kähler manifold has a well-behaved analytic structure.
analysis.main_result: Let \(\mathcal F\) have dimension \(k\) on a compact Kähler manifold \(M\) of dimension \(n\). Assume regular leaf volumes are uniformly bounded, \(\dim(\operatorname{Sing}\mathcal F)<k\), and the union of leaf closures meeting the singular set has finite \(2k\)-dimensional Hausdorff measure. The quotient by chains of intersecting leaf closures is normal, compact and complex analytic of dimension \(n-k\); its map is proper and holomorphic with connected fibers. Away from separatrix images there are local charts from finite holonomy groups. Examples show that these images need not equal the quotient’s singular set and that bounded volumes alone do not imply Hausdorffness. In codimension one the measure assumption is automatic when the singular set has codimension at least three, by Malgrange’s theorem.
methods: Malgrange’s theorem in the stated codimension-one case
analysis.context: Singular holomorphic foliations, analytic quotients and leaf-closure topology.

paper.title: Arithmeticity, superrigidity, and totally geodesic submanifolds of infinite-volume hyperbolic manifolds
paper.abstract: Given an infinite-volume convex cocompact hyperbolic manifold with Fuchsian ends and infinitely many maximal properly immersed totally geodesic submanifolds of dimension at least two intersecting its convex core, we show that it (infinitely) covers an arithmetic hyperbolic manifold. This answers the general version of a question of Oh. As a byproduct of our techniques, we also give a Ratner-type classification of $\mathrm{SO}_0(m,1)$-invariant Radon measures whose support intersects the frame bundle of the interior of the convex core.

analysis.relevance_note: Arithmetic rigidity of hyperbolic manifolds and a classification of invariant Radon measures provide strong connections to homogeneous dynamics and group actions.
analysis.tldr: The authors prove arithmetic covering rigidity for certain infinite-volume convex cocompact hyperbolic manifolds with Fuchsian ends and infinitely many specified totally geodesic submanifolds. They also obtain a Ratner-type classification of invariant Radon measures with the stated support restriction.
analysis.problem: Relate abundance of maximal properly immersed totally geodesic submanifolds to arithmeticity for infinite-volume hyperbolic manifolds.
analysis.main_result: An infinite-volume convex cocompact hyperbolic manifold with Fuchsian ends and infinitely many maximal properly immersed totally geodesic submanifolds of dimension at least two intersecting its convex core infinitely covers an arithmetic hyperbolic manifold. The abstract states this answers the general version of Oh’s question. A byproduct is a Ratner-type classification of \(\mathrm{SO}_0(m,1)\)-invariant Radon measures whose support meets the frame bundle of the interior of the convex core; the classification alternatives are not given. Further method details: Not specified in the abstract.
analysis.context: Hyperbolic geometry, arithmeticity, homogeneous dynamics and invariant measures.

paper.title: Training-Induced Escape from Token Clustering in a Mean-Field Formulation of Transformers
paper.abstract: Transformers perform inference by iteratively transforming token representations across layers. This layerwise computation has been studied empirically, and recent mean-field theories of Transformer dynamics explain how attention can drive token distributions toward clustering. However, existing analyses treat model parameters as prescribed, leaving open how training reshapes this clustering picture. We study this question in a noisy mean-field Transformer in which only a parameter-linear FFN is trained under $L^2$ regularization. We identify a training-induced phase of the inference dynamics across layers: after clustering in the early layers, the token distribution can leave the clustered regime near the final layers. A single gradient-descent update already produces this escape, and minimizers of the training objective satisfy an exponential turnpike bound under which clustering persists through the interior layers. Our analysis is based on an entropy-regularized interaction energy that captures the clustering bias of attention, for which we establish a double-well landscape and a local Polyak-{\L}ojasiewicz inequality. More broadly, our results point toward a training-aware mean-field theory in which training and inference dynamics of Transformers are treated together.

analysis.relevance_note: The focus is training and clustering in mean-field Transformer models; entropy regularization is used, but no central result on dynamical entropy or the other strongest interests is stated.

paper.title: The Martin boundary of the Directed Landscape
paper.abstract: In the directed landscape, the Martin boundary coincides with the horofunction boundary. We show that functions in this boundary are precisely the eternal solutions possessing a spatial growth rate, and that the minimal Martin boundary is given by the Busemann functions. Moreover, every eternal solution can be expressed as a max-plus convex combination of countably many Busemann functions. Horofunctions are exactly those eternal solutions that admit a representation in terms of at most two Busemann functions with a common growth rate. As a consequence of instability, not all horofunctions are Busemann functions, and the Martin boundary is strictly larger than its minimal part.

analysis.relevance_note: Boundary representations and eternal solutions give a possible geometric and topological connection, although entropy, fractal dimension and group actions are not central in the abstract.
analysis.tldr: In the directed landscape the Martin and horofunction boundaries coincide, while the minimal Martin boundary consists of Busemann functions. The authors characterize boundary functions and representations of eternal solutions.
analysis.problem: Identify the Martin, minimal Martin and horofunction boundaries of the directed landscape through eternal solutions and Busemann functions.
analysis.main_result: The boundary functions are precisely eternal solutions possessing a spatial growth rate, and the minimal Martin boundary consists of Busemann functions. Every eternal solution is a max-plus convex combination of countably many Busemann functions. Horofunctions are exactly the eternal solutions represented by at most two Busemann functions with a common growth rate. Instability implies that some horofunctions are not Busemann functions and the Martin boundary is strictly larger than its minimal part.
analysis.context: Directed landscape, geometric boundaries and max-plus representations of eternal solutions.

paper.title: Differentiability of the Leading Lyapunov Exponent of a linear differential equation with random coefficients Application to the Calculation of the Selection Gradient in Random Environments
paper.abstract: The study of evolution in temporally fluctuating environments often relies on the analysis of Lyapunov exponents, which quantify the exponential growth of populations. However, when model parameters depend on a stochastic process, calculating the selection gradient, a key tool for predicting the evolution of phenotypic traits, becomes a mathematical challenge. While the periodic case has been resolved, a general approach for random environments remains to be developed. This article proposes a rigorous method to: Establish the differentiability of the leading Lyapunov exponent with respect to a parameter, providing an explicit integral formula for its derivative. Develop a numerical algorithm to approximate the derivative by solving an extended differential equation. Apply these results to the analysis of mutant invasion in a resident population at equilibrium, identifying the selection gradient as the derivative of the top Lyapunov exponent.

analysis.relevance_note: Parameter response of random Lyapunov exponents connects to random dynamics, although the application is population evolution and no entropy or dimension theorem is stated.
analysis.tldr: The authors propose a rigorous method for differentiating the leading Lyapunov exponent of a linear differential equation with random coefficients, together with a numerical derivative algorithm and a selection-gradient application.
analysis.problem: Compute parameter derivatives of leading Lyapunov exponents when coefficients depend on a stochastic process, in order to study selection gradients in fluctuating environments.
analysis.main_result: The abstract describes a method establishing differentiability with an explicit integral derivative formula and approximating the derivative by an extended differential equation. Applied to mutant invasion in a resident population at equilibrium, the selection gradient is identified with the derivative of the top Lyapunov exponent. The precise regularity and stochastic hypotheses and integral formula: Not specified in the abstract.
methods: Explicit integral formula for the Lyapunov-exponent derivative
Numerical solution of an extended differential equation
analysis.context: Random linear differential equations, Lyapunov response and evolutionary population dynamics.
